country.comment: Data are drawn from five rural piped water operators working across five regions in Ghana, 12 districts in Rwanda, and nine districts (eight by one social enterprise and one by two private companies) in Uganda.
country.where_found: PDF Page 2, Abstract; PDF Page 5, Section 2.1; PDF Page 8, Table 1 and Figure 3

effect_estimate.comment: Exact GEE regression estimates (Table 5) and descriptive usage/revenue statistics (Table 4) reported across all four service area archetypes.
effect_estimate.value: In GEE regressions of log-transformed volumetric revenue ($/m3) across 4 rural piped water service area archetypes (2016–2019), volumetric revenue is significantly and positively associated with tariff level in all archetypes: Multi-country (β = 0.470, 95% CI [0.407, 0.532], p < 0.001), Single-country Uganda (β = 0.399, 95% CI [0.301, 0.498], p < 0.001), Enterprise-led (β = 0.371, 95% CI [0.229, 0.512], p < 0.001), and Public-led (β = 0.493, 95% CI [0.402, 0.584], p < 0.001). Controlling for tariff level, on-premises connections do not differ significantly in volumetric revenue from off-premises connections in any archetype (Multi-country: β = −0.034, 95% CI [−0.118, 0.050], p = 0.429; Single-country: β = −0.119, 95% CI [−0.276, 0.038], p = 0.139; Enterprise: β = −0.040, 95% CI [−0.380, 0.301], p = 0.820; Public: β = −0.080, 95% CI [−0.188, 0.028], p = 0.148). Controlling for tariff level, prepaid credit payment systems do not yield higher volumetric revenue than conventional pay-as-you-fetch (PAYF) or monthly billing in Archetypes 1–3 (Multi-country: β = −0.075, 95% CI [−0.210, 0.061], p = 0.279; Single-country: β = −0.071, 95% CI [−0.187, 0.044], p = 0.227; Enterprise: β = −0.442, 95% CI [−0.952, 0.068], p = 0.089) and show a slight negative association in Public-led Archetype 4 (β = −0.166, 95% CI [−0.248, −0.084], p < 0.001, based on <4% of archetype records). Off-premises standpipes and kiosks dispense higher monthly water volumes per waterpoint than on-premises connections in all archetypes (Multi-country: 55.42 vs 13.52 m3/waterpoint/month; Single-country: 19.88 vs 5.95; Enterprise: 69.97 vs 7.48; Public: 32.23 vs 17.76) and generate greater total monthly revenue per service area in three of four archetypes (Multi-country: $538 vs $319; Enterprise: $752 vs $302; Public: $381 vs $324; Single-country: $235 vs $378).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by observational longitudinal design (JBI Cohort). Assigned 1 (documented association) because the study establishes statistical and descriptive associations across aggregate monthly operator records between tariff levels, payment collection modalities, connection types, investment/governance archetypes, waterpoint volumes dispensed, and volumetric revenue, while explicitly noting that household-level user counts, service penetration, and actual retail prices paid to attendants are unobserved (Section 4.2, PDF p. 15; Section 4.4, PDF p. 16).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF Page 7, Section 2.3; PDF Page 12, Section 3.4; PDF Page 13, Table 5; PDF Pages 15–17, Sections 4.2–4.4

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines volumetric tariffs, one-off connection fees, and payment collection modalities (PAYF, monthly billing, prepaid credit) [BURDEN: fees], alongside piped service area delineation/population-density thresholds and public vs enterprise infrastructure planning and contracting strategies for blending on- and off-premises connections [ELIGIBILITY: service_area, planning].
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF Pages 5–7, Sections 2.1–2.2; PDF Pages 7–8, Section 3.1 and Table 1; PDF Pages 14–16, Sections 4.2–4.3

outcome_flags.comment: Directly analyses on-premises vs off-premises piped waterpoints (formal_connection, water_access), monthly water volume dispensed per waterpoint in m3/waterpoint/month (service_quantity), and tariff levels/payment modalities/affordability trade-offs for rural users (affordability). Scheme reliability, water quality, and sanitation are not measured in the dataset.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Observational longitudinal repeated-measures study tracking piped water service areas over at least 12 months (2016–2019) using GEE panel models with autoregressive correlation, without a quasi-experimental intervention or policy-shock comparator (ruling out ROBINS-I) and using longitudinal rather than cross-sectional data (selecting JBI Cohort over JBI Cross-Sectional; unstructured interviews with operator data specialists were solely for cleaning/validating secondary quantitative records rather than a primary qualitative research component).
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

sample_size.comment: Full cleaned dataset (Archetype 1: Multi-country) comprises 5 operators, 220 split/homogenised service areas (96 off-premises + 124 on-premises), 3,941 waterpoints (867 off-premises + 3,074 on-premises), and 3,903 monthly tariff records (1,697 off-premises + 2,206 on-premises; 3,891 monthly volume records; 3,774 monthly revenue records) spanning 2016–2019, plus iterative unstructured data-validation interviews with data specialists from the 5 operators.
sample_size.value: 5 piped water operators; 220 service areas (96 off-premises, 124 on-premises); 3,941 waterpoints (867 off-premises, 3,074 on-premises); 3,903 monthly tariff records (3,891 volume records; 3,774 revenue records) from 2016 to 2019
sample_size.where_found: PDF Page 2, Abstract; PDF Page 5, Section 2.1; PDF Page 8, Table 1; PDF Page 10, Table 3

study_design.comment: Authors construct four rural piped water service area archetypes (Multi-country, Single-country Uganda, Enterprise-led, Public-led) from secondary monthly operational records (each spanning >=12 months between 2016 and 2019, validated via unstructured interviews with operator data specialists) and estimate population-averaged effects using GEE models with autoregressive correlation structures and leave-one-out sensitivity checks.
study_design.value: Multi-country longitudinal observational study combining service area archetype analysis (ANOVA and Student's t-tests) with generalized estimating equations (GEE) repeated-measures panel regression of secondary monthly operator records (2016–2019)
study_design.where_found: PDF Pages 5–7, Sections 2.1–2.3; PDF Page 9, Table 2; PDF Page 13, Table 5
